target: Redan som barn älskade hon att sjunga och dansa.
english: Already as a child she loved to sing and dance.
tip: In questions with a question word, V2 still applies: question word + verb + subject.

target: Min familj bor i en liten stad i södern.
english: My family lives in a small town in the south.
tip: 'Liten' is highly irregular: en→liten, ett→litet, definite→lilla, plural→små.

target: Skynda dig så att vi inte missar bussen dit!
english: Hurry up so we don't miss the bus!
tip: In subordinate clauses, `inte` moves before the verb: `att jag inte äter pizza` (that I don't eat pizza). Compare to the main-clause order `jag äter inte pizza`.

target: Barnen sov djupt hela natten och vaknade tidigt imorse.
english: The children slept deeply all night and woke up early this morning.
tip: Group 4 verbs change vowels instead of adding endings: dricka → drack (drink → drank), gå → gick (go → went), se → såg (see → saw). Common irregulars.

target: Jag har en fråga om de nya parkeringsreglerna i stadskärnan.
english: I have a question about the new parking regulations in the city centre.
tip: "Fråga" is both a noun (en fråga) and a verb (att fråga). Very common.

target: Validiteten i studien kan ifrågasättas.
english: The validity of the study can be questioned.
tip: "Ifrågasätta" = question/challenge. Essential critical thinking verb.

target: Vi bör vara försiktiga med generaliseringar.
english: We should be cautious with generalizations.
tip: If you see a 15-letter word, don't panic. It's almost certainly 2-3 words glued together. Read left to right, find the main noun on the right.

target: Det verkar bra hela tiden med vänner.
english: It seems good all the time with friends.
tip: Definite form adjectives add "-a": "den stora bilen" (the big car).

target: Snart kommer sommaren under sommaren till slut.
english: Soon summer will come during the summer in the end.
tip: "Snart" = soon. Fronted adverb triggers V2 inversion.

target: De samlar på gamla böcker och har en stor samling.
english: They collect old books and have a large collection.
tip: 'Stor' (big): en-word: 'en stor stad', ett-word: 'ett stort hus', definite/plural: 'den stora staden'.

target: Det kan inte stämma.
english: That can't be right.
tip: `inte` (not) goes after the verb in main clauses: `jag äter inte pizza` (I don't eat pizza). Watch the position – putting `inte` first is wrong.

target: Sex, sju, åtta, nio, tio.
english: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
tip: "Sju" (7) contains the tricky sj-sound [ɧ]. "Åtta" has double-t making the å short.

target: Hon undrade var vi bodde.
english: She wondered where we lived.
tip: Reported questions with wh-words keep the question word: var, när, hur, etc.

target: Jag är tjugofem år gammal.
english: I am twenty-five years old.
tip: 'Gammal' (old): ett→gammalt, definite/plural→gamla. Irregular but very common.

target: Den stora bilen är min.
english: The big car is mine.
tip: Double definite: adjective + definite article (den/det/de) and definite suffix (-en/-et/-na).

target: Vem har nyckeln under veckan alltid?
english: Who has the key during the week always?
tip: When the question word IS the subject, no inversion: Vem + verb.

target: Hur länge har du bott här redan?
english: How long have you lived here already?
tip: Swedish has two genders: "en" (common) and "ett" (neuter).

target: Vad rekommenderar du efter jobbet till slut?
english: What do you recommend doing after work?
tip: "Rekommendera" is borrowed from French/Latin – common in Swedish.

target: Han frågade om jag hade lust att följa med ut.
english: He asked if I felt like coming along.
tip: Reported questions use "om" (if/whether) for yes/no questions.

target: Midsommar firas i juni.
english: Midsummer is celebrated in June.
tip: Midsummer falls on the Friday between June 19-25. Not always the 24th.

target: Filmjölken serveras med knäckebröd.
english: The filmjölk is served with crispbread.
tip: Knäckebröd (crispbread) is a Swedish staple found in every household.

target: Köttbullar med lingon och potatis.
english: Meatballs with lingonberries and potatoes.
tip: Köttbullar med lingon is perhaps Sweden's most iconic dish.

target: Lagom bra tillsammans för alla verkligen.
english: Moderately good together for everyone really.
tip: "Lagom" – not too good, not too bad, just the right amount.

target: Vi undrar om det finns plats här.
english: We wonder if there's space here.
tip: "Om" introduces indirect yes/no questions: 'We wonder if/whether there's room.'

target: Har du varit i Sverige förut väl?
english: Have you been to Sweden before?
tip: "Förut" = before/previously. Placed at the end of the sentence.

target: Äntligen har vi kommit fram till vårt mål nu.
english: Finally we have reached our goal now.
tip: "Äntligen" = finally/at last. Expresses relief after a long wait.

target: Det känns skönt att vara hemma igen efter resan.
english: It feels nice to be home again after the trip.
tip: Question word + verb + subject. The verb must always be in second position.

target: Kan du rekommendera en bra bok att läsa i sommar?
english: Can you recommend a good book to read this summer?
tip: 'Kan' (can) – doesn't change form. The main verb stays infinitive: 'Jag kan simma' (I can swim).

target: Vad synd att du inte kunde komma med oss idag!
english: What a shame that you could not come with us today!
tip: After att, när, om, eftersom: inte (not) goes before the verb. Jag vet att han inte kommer (I know that he isn't coming).

target: Filmjölk smakar gott med flingor.
english: Soured milk tastes good with cereal.
tip: Filmjölk is a fermented dairy product unique to Scandinavia.

target: Han är lärare.
english: He is a teacher.
tip: Swedish expressions often use 'tack' (thanks/please) – it's the Swiss army knife of Swedish politeness.

target: Smörgåsen är god.
english: The sandwich is good.
tip: "Smörgås" is quintessentially Swedish – an open-faced sandwich with various toppings.

target: Vi somnade sent.
english: We fell asleep late.
tip: When an adverb starts the sentence, subject and verb swap: "Idag åker jag" = Today I go.

target: Jag har ingen aning.
english: I have no idea.
tip: "Aning" = idea/inkling. "Ingen aning" = no idea.

target: De vackra blommorna doftar gott.
english: The beautiful flowers smell nice.
tip: "Dofta" = smell (emit scent). "Gott" (neuter) here because it's an adverb, not adjective.

target: Jag tar en portion pytt i panna.
english: I'll have a portion of hash.
tip: Pytt i panna is a classic Swedish dish – diced potatoes, meat, and onions fried together.

target: Den svarta katten sitter i fönstret på jobbet.
english: The black cat sits in the window at work.
tip: Double definite with en-word: den + svarta + katten. Adjective always ends in -a in definite.

target: Janssons frestelse till julbordet.
english: Jansson's Temptation for the Christmas table.
tip: A classic Swedish potato and anchovy casserole served at Christmas.

target: Dillsåsen serveras till fisken.
english: Dill sauce is served with the fish.
tip: Dill is perhaps the most important herb in Swedish cooking.

target: De svenska somrarna är korta.
english: The Swedish summers are short.
tip: "Kort" → "korta" in plural/definite. "Svensk" → "svenska" – same pattern for all adjectives.

target: Flickan med det röda håret.
english: The girl with the red hair.
tip: "Hår" is ett-word: "det röda håret" – double definite with adjective.

target: Prinsesstårtan är grön och god.
english: The princess cake is green and delicious.
tip: Prinsesstårta (green marzipan-covered cake) is Sweden's national cake.

target: Sillen på julbordet är traditionell.
english: The herring at the Christmas table is traditional.
tip: Julbordet (Christmas buffet) features many varieties of pickled herring.

target: Skit samma, vi gör det på vårt sätt istället.
english: Whatever, we will do it our way instead.
tip: Mildly vulgar but extremely common in casual Swedish.

target: Vad tråkigt att höra att du inte mår bra.
english: Sorry to hear you're not feeling well.
tip: After att, när, om, eftersom: inte (not) goes before the verb. Jag vet att han inte kommer (I know that he isn't coming).

target: En ny restaurang har öppnat alldeles runt hörnet från oss.
english: A new restaurant has opened just around the corner from us.
tip: Swedish future uses "ska" (will/shall) or "kommer att" (going to).

target: Det var länge sedan jag pratade svenska med någon annan.
english: It was a long time since I spoke Swedish with someone else.
tip: 'Var' is past tense of 'vara' (was): same for all persons. 'Jag var', 'du var', 'vi var'.

target: Det är så skönt att komma hem efter en lång arbetsdag.
english: It is so nice to come home after a long workday.
tip: Swedish adjective agreement: en-form (base), ett-form (+t), definite/plural (+a): 'fin/fint/fina'.

target: Duktig som hon är löser hon allt.
english: Skilled as she is, she solves everything.
tip: Adjective fronting for emphasis: adjective + som + subject + verb.

target: Hej, en fråga bara på kvällen nästa år.
english: Hi, just a question in the evening next year.
tip: Casual opener – very common in everyday Swedish.

target: Jag längtar.
english: I long for it.
tip: "Längta" expresses yearning or longing – a deeply Swedish word with no exact English match.

target: Vi beställde pizza.
english: We ordered pizza.
tip: Swedish V2 rule: the verb is always second in main clauses.

target: Han rastar hunden.
english: He walks the dog.
tip: "Rasta" specifically means to take the dog out – not just any walk.

target: Det återstår att se.
english: It remains to be seen.
tip: "Återstå" = remain. Very common phrase meaning the outcome is uncertain.

target: Vi drog oss tillbaka tidigt.
english: We pulled back early.
tip: Object pronouns: mig (me), dig (you), honom (him), henne (her), oss (us), er (you pl), dem (them). Place after the verb: `jag ser dig`.

target: Självklart kommer jag att vara där på festen.
english: Of course I will be there at the party.
tip: "Självklart" = of course! Compound: "själv" (self) + "klart" (clear). Very common.

target: Han delar med sig av sina kunskaper till alla nya medarbetare.
english: He shares his knowledge with all new coworkers.
tip: 'Sig' is the reflexive for han/hon/de: 'Han tvättar sig' (He washes himself).

target: Lagom är bäst.
english: Moderation is best.
tip: "Lagom är bäst" – the unofficial Swedish motto. Just the right amount is ideal.

target: Hon hävdade att det var sant.
english: She maintained that it was true.
tip: "Hävda" (claim/maintain) – a formal reporting verb. Everyday: "sa" (said).

target: Det var som fan efter jobbet egentligen!
english: That was unbelievable after work actually!
tip: Mildly vulgar exclamation expressing astonishment.
